thesis: Ligand Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: LGND), royalty and Captisol licensing company. Closed the XOMA Royalty acquisition on 2026-07-14 (cash paid net 782.9M in 9M26 per 10-Q), more than doubling royalty assets to over 200. Q3 2026: total revenue 78.7M (-32% because Q3 2025 had 53.1M Pelthos income; +26% excluding it), royalties 70.3M (+51%), GAAP net loss 28.5M (-1.43 per share) after 35.7M investment fair value loss and 72.6M G&A including 23.9M transaction and integration costs; adjusted EPS 2.67 (-14%). 2026 guidance: royalty 225-250M, total revenue 270-310M, adjusted EPS raised to about 9.50-9.75 from 9.00-9.50. At 308.79 (2026-11-13 close; 52-week 175.89-326.63; market cap about 6.18B) trailing GAAP P/E is about 124x, about 32x the adjusted EPS guide midpoint, TTM FCF 90.7M is a 1.5% yield (0.55% after SBC), and net debt is about 0.71B (1.16B convertible principal less 447M cash and short-term investments). The market is paying for royalty growth from XOMA, Filspari and Ohtuvayre and a long royalty runway; the evidence for that is real but the price already embeds much of it.
counterthesis: Valuation is the problem: 124x GAAP and 24x sales with a 1.5% FCF yield. The gap between adjusted EPS (about 9.6) and GAAP (about 2.5 TTM) comes from SBC (56.7M TTM, 42.4M in 9M26), intangible amortization, deal costs and fair value marks that recur for an acquisitive royalty buyer. Leverage rose from 0.45B to 1.16B principal; cash fell to 447M from 734M. The stock is only about 5% below its 52-week high and analysts have been raising targets. Revenue concentration in a few royalties (Filspari, Ohtuvayre, Vabysmo) and patent or competitive loss, integration cost overruns and a failed capital allocation would break the thesis. Forms 144 sales appear frequently in submissions (content unread).
invalidation: Thesis breaks if royalty revenue growth stalls below guidance, adjusted EPS guide is cut, Ohtuvayre or Filspari royalties fall materially, XOMA integration costs or contingent liabilities grow, or leverage rises without matching royalty income.
